QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_15

question.text: Which of the following lists contains ONLY valid Category I AIF sub-categories as defined under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012?

answer.text: Venture Capital Fund, SME Fund, Private Equity Fund, Infrastructure Fund
Venture Capital Fund, SME Fund, Angel Fund, Infrastructure Fund, Social Impact Fund, Special Situations Fund
Venture Capital Fund, Hedge Fund, Private Equity Fund, Debt Fund
Angel Fund, Hedge Fund, Special Situations Fund, Corporate Debt Market Development Fund

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 6.2.12, Category I AIFs include Venture Capital Funds, SME Funds, Angel Funds, Social Impact Funds, Infrastructure Funds, Special Situation Funds, and the Corporate Debt Market Development Fund (CDMDF). Private Equity Funds and Debt Funds fall under Cat II; Hedge Funds fall under Cat III. **The Trap:** Option A wrongly includes PE (Cat II). Option C mixes PE/Debt (Cat II) and Hedge (Cat III) into Cat I. Option D wrongly includes Hedge Funds (Cat III) — though it correctly includes Angel, SSF and CDMDF. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A Cat I/II Distributor exam tests the sub-category taxonomy closely; XIX-C adds the operational significance of category election for leverage/concentration treatment. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** At registration, the SEBI application asks you to pick sub-category; picking the wrong one (e.g., tagging an SSF as a pure PE Cat II fund) forfeits the Cat I incentive framework and is painful to reverse — map your investee universe to the sub-category definitions BEFORE filing.
